newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenia's foreign firms more profitable - report.
newsitem.headline: Slovenia's foreign firms more profitable - report.

text.p: Slovenian companies that are in partial or full foreign ownership are more profitable than domestic firms, the state-owned Institute of Macroeconomic Analysis and Development said on Tuesday.

"In 1994 investment firms with foreign investment accounted for only 6.6 percent of non-financial corporate sector equity but made 15.6 percent of the sector's profit," Matija Rojec, researcher at the institute said, adding that the figures probably still held true.

Rojec said the research, recently performed by the institute, concentrated on non-financial corporate firms that were at least 10 percent foreign owned. He said there were 1,128 such firms, representing 3.6 percent of all companies in the sector.
According to Rojec, foreign companies were more profitable mainly because they enjoyed easier access to foreign markets and to fresh capital.
"Their exports represented 19.1 percent of total export in the sector," he said.

Foreign direct investment in Slovenia in 1995 rose to $l76 million, or 0.9 percent of the country's gross domestic product aPLGDP, from $83.7 million in 1994. However, experts said further growth in 1996 was unlikely.
"There is no reason for an increase as there are no incentives for foreign investors," Rojec said.

He said, however, an increase could be expected at the end of 1997 or in 1998, once the government's massive privatisation process is finished and newly privatised companies start to look for foreign partners.

The voucher privatisation process, which started in 1994, includes about 1,500 companies and is expected to finish at the end of 1997. Some 730 companies have already been privatised. -- Marja Novak, Ljubljana newsroom, 386-61-125-8439
